With 44 places separating them in FIFA’s rankings, UEFA Nations League (UNL) Group C2 brings together 80th-ranked Montenegro and 124th-ranked Cyprus with both teams entering the tournament in decent form.

Match News and Current Form

Montenegro spent the last two editions of the UNL in League B, but five defeats from six games (W1) in that division in 2024/25 saw them relegated. That sees the Brave Falcons return to League C where they spent the first two UNL tournaments, and whether coach Mirko Vučinić and his side get their 2026/27 campaign off to a positive start seems to be a coin toss, given only three of their 24 prior UNL encounters ended in a draw (W9, L12). That’s actually been a theme not just in the UNL for Montenegro, with just two stalemates across their last 29 international matches overall after a 2-2 draw with Slovenia last time out, a result preceded by four wins in their six matches prior (L2).

Cyprus have been ever-present in League C, and they’ll be hoping it’s third time lucky as they’re drawn in Group C2 for the third consecutive instalment. Akis Mantzios’s men possess a three-game unbeaten streak in friendly internationals this year (W2, D1), but their hopes of getting off to a positive start seem slim as they’ve won their opening UNL match just once in the past four editions (L3). Hitting the road also presents an issue as they’ve won just one of their prior 12 UNL away games (D3, L8), while they last beat a team ranked above them way back in November 2022 when overcoming Israel!

Head-to-Head History

Montenegro haven’t lost any of their five matches against Cyprus (W2, D3), winning the last two meetings and keeping a clean sheet in the last three.

Hot Stats and Streaks

Seven of Montenegro’s last nine matches saw over 2.5 match goals.

Montenegro have scored exactly twice in five of their last six home games.

Nine of Cyprus’ last ten games saw goals in both halves.

Just one of Cyprus’ last five away matches saw both teams score.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Stevan Jovetić , Montenegro’s most capped player (91) and top goalscorer (37) who now plays in the Cypriot First Division, will hope to get Montenegro off to a good start again after netting their opener in four of his last five goalscoring appearances. Cyprus’ Ioannis Pittas might have a say in this game, since four of his last six national goals came on the road.

Montenegro are missing the likes of Sead Hakšabanović and Andrija Ražnatović through injury, while Cyprus midfielder Charalampos Charalampous was not selected for this international window.

Betting Analysis

Both teams will look to get forward and impose themselves, meaning both teams to score and over 2.5 goals seems worth a look here.
